prompts.text: Write a short thank-you note to someone you have not yet thanked and would like to acknowledge. (We encourage you to share this note with that person, if possible, and reflect on the experience!)
How will you explore community at Penn? Consider how Penn will help shape your perspective, and how your experiences and perspective will help shape Penn.

Penn Nursing intends to meet the health needs of society in a global and multicultural world by preparing its students to impact healthcare by advancing science. Why are you applying to Nursing, where do you see yourself professionally in the future, and how will you contribute to our mission of promoting equity in healthcare?
prompts.applies_to: School of Nursing single-degree applicants (also the single-degree school choice of NHCM applicants who select Nursing)

prompts.text: The College of Arts and Sciences is designed to foster discovery and connection. Describe something you are curious about—something you'd like to learn more about or find a new approach to—and how you might pursue that curiosity in the College.
prompts.applies_to: College of Arts and Sciences single-degree applicants (including dual-degree/specialized program applicants whose single-degree choice is the College)

prompts.text: Wharton prepares its students to make an impact by applying business methods and economic theory to real-world problems, including economic, political, and social issues. Discuss a current issue of importance to you and how you hope a Wharton education would help you explore it.
prompts.applies_to: The Wharton School single-degree applicants (including dual-degree/specialized program applicants whose single-degree choice is Wharton)

prompts.text: Penn Engineering prepares its students to become leaders in technology by combining a strong foundation in the natural sciences and mathematics with depth of study in focused disciplinary majors. Describe how you plan to pursue your engineering interests at Penn, particularly within the intended major you selected.
prompts.applies_to: Penn Engineering (School of Engineering and Applied Science) single-degree applicants (including dual-degree/specialized program applicants whose single-degree choice is Engineering)

prompts.text: Applicants to the Huntsman Program in International Studies and Business must choose one of eleven target languages. Please select your target language.
prompts.applies_to: Huntsman Program in International Studies and Business applicants only (selection of one of eleven target languages, not an essay)

prompts.text: Describe your experience with the target language you selected. You may wish to share the length of time you’ve studied or used this language, how you’ve learned it, the skills you’ve acquired, and/or the skills you still wish to develop. Please also explain why you are interested in studying this language and the region(s) of the world where it is spoken.
prompts.applies_to: Huntsman Program in International Studies and Business applicants only

prompts.text: The Huntsman Program supports the development of globally-minded scholars who become engaged citizens, creative innovators, and ethical leaders in the public, private, and non-profit sectors in the United States and around the world. What draws you to a dual degree in international studies and business, and how would you use what you learn to address a global issue where these two domains intersect?
prompts.applies_to: Huntsman Program in International Studies and Business applicants only

prompts.text: The Vagelos Life Sciences & Management (LSM) program brings together two powerful modes of understanding—scientific inquiry and strategic thinking—to prepare students to engage thoughtfully and creatively with some of the most complex challenges of our time. What questions, problems, or opportunities would you hope to explore through LSM, and how might the integration of life sciences and management shape your approach to them? Focus on the ideas, values, or questions that draw you to this intersection, rather than how LSM might advance your career, and make sure this essay is distinct from your single-degree application.
prompts.applies_to: Roy and Diana Vagelos Program in Life Sciences and Management (LSM) applicants only

prompts.text: Explain how you will use the M&T program to pursue problems or opportunities that require both engineering and business perspectives.
prompts.applies_to: Jerome Fisher Program in Management and Technology (M&T) applicants only

prompts.text: Describe something you created, designed, improved, or built. What motivated you, and what did you learn from the process?
prompts.applies_to: Jerome Fisher Program in Management and Technology (M&T) applicants only

prompts.text: Describe your interest in nursing and health care management, and how Penn's coordinated dual-degree program in nursing and business would help you meet your goals. Please ensure that this essay is distinct from your single-degree application, if applicable.
prompts.applies_to: Nursing and Healthcare Management (NHCM) coordinated dual-degree applicants only

prompts.text: VIPER students pursue dual degrees in science or math and engineering. Which major combination(s) interest you most right now and why? Your response to this prompt is not binding; students often shift majors as they learn more through the program. See available VIPER majors on our website.
prompts.applies_to: Roy and Diana Vagelos Integrated Program in Energy Research (VIPER) applicants only

prompts.text: Describe your interest in the VIPER program, including how any past experiences (academic, research, extracurricular, etc.) have shaped your interest in energy science and technology, and how you envision participation in VIPER fitting into your future goals.
prompts.applies_to: Roy and Diana Vagelos Integrated Program in Energy Research (VIPER) applicants only

prompts.text: Discuss how your interests align with the Visual and Interactive Computing (VIC) program at the University of Pennsylvania
prompts.applies_to: BSE in Visual and Interactive Computing (VIC) applicants only

prompts.text: Please explain your reasons for transferring from your current institution and what you hope to gain by transferring to another institution.
prompts.applies_to: transfer applicants only (not first-year); also capped at 2,000 characters

notes: Official page is headed '2026-27 Short Answer and Essay Prompts'. Every applicant answers the two all-applicant prompts plus ONE school-specific prompt for their single-degree school choice (Nursing, College of Arts and Sciences, Wharton, or Engineering). Coordinated dual-degree/specialized program applicants (Huntsman, LSM, M&T, NHCM, VIPER, VIC) additionally answer their program-specific prompts. Limits are stated on the page as '(50-200 words)', '(50 to 200 words)', '(50-400 words)' etc.; recorded as word_min 50 and word_limit 200/400. The trailing limit parentheticals were removed from 'text'; all other wording is copied exactly (HTML non-breaking/double spaces normalized to single spaces). Each school/program prompt is followed on the page by a 'To help inform your response, we encourage you to review...' guidance line, which is not included in 'text'. Huntsman upenn-7 is a target-language selection (one of eleven languages), counted by Penn as one of the three Huntsman responses; it is not a written essay. upenn-17 (transfer essay) applies only to transfer applicants: '(50-400 words/up to 2,000 characters)'. The page says double-asterisk numbers denote character counts for transfer Common App applicants; none appeared on first-year prompts. upenn-16 (VIC) has no terminal period in text because on the page the period follows the limit: "...University of Pennsylvania (50-400 words)."
